content.text:
Let me analyze this ticket.

Employee: Maurice Perez (E036)
Request: write access to Source Code

Two conflicting notes:
- HR note: full_time Engineer, recommends write
- Security note: contractor, basic security training, recommends read

Access policy:
1. full_time employees: up to write. Admin only if role owns system.
2. contractor employees: read, or write if advanced security training. Never admin.

Role: Engineer owns Source Code system. So if full-time, write is allowed (up to write, admin max but requested write). If contractor with basic training, max is read.

The two notes conflict on employment type and security training. Security DB is presumably more authoritative for contractor status/security training? The note says "Security DB shows..." vs HR. Typically security is authoritative for contractor status and training. The Security note says contractor with basic training, so maximum is read. Requested write exceeds maximum, so grant read.

I should decide based on the available facts. The conflicting evidence: HR says full-time, Security says contractor. Which to trust? The security agent has security DB. I think the security note is the more reliable for access control purposes. Grant read.

Let me submit decision: read, with reason citing contractor status per security DB, basic training, max read, requested write exceeds max.
